thread.title: Day 1 Of 'Retirement' And The Dividends Arrive As A Sign From Above - Enbridge Inc. (NYSE:ENB)

author: Dale Roberts
title: Day 1 Of 'Retirement' And The Dividends Arrive As A Sign From Above - Enbridge Inc. (NYSE:ENB)
text:
Last Thursday May 31, 2018 was my last day of full time work. I left a job and coworkers that I really enjoyed. It's a semi retirement or new work life stage. In the retirement biz they would call it an early retirement by Design. I wrote on the event with Saying Goodbye To Your Pay Cheque: It Ain't Easy . And then inspired by the comments and insights of Seeking Alpha readers, many who were retirees or early retirees, I offered Planning and Enjoying an Early Retirement? Seeking Alpha Readers Say Yes, Yes and Yes!
Well I said to goodbye to that pay cheque on May 31, and on June 1 I said hello to my first retirement dividends courtesy of Enbridge ( ENB ). Enbridge is one of the big dividend payers in My Canadian Wide Moat 7 .
Of course utilities have come under great pressure recently with what many feel is a 'sure' rising rate environment. Those bigger bond payments can compete for the utility investor's or dividend income investor's monies, and those monies can leave the big dividend payers for the land of 'safer' bond coupon payments. Also, utilities can carry large debts to fund projects, and with higher borrowing costs comes lesser funds available for dividends and dividend growth. Throw in a regulatory hits and uncertainty and the pipeline sub sector has been taken down considerably. Enbridge has also recently completed a more than sizeable takeover of Spectra Energy. They've acquired more debt and analysts and fund managers are not sure of how Enbridge can absorb the new debt and acquisition and keep those dividends flowing and growing. Those events have taken Enbridge for a ride, and mostly to the downside.
Courtesy of portfoliovisualizer.com, here's the recent price total returns history of Enbridge from January of 2017 to end of May 2018. The chart is from the TSE Toronto Stock Exchange listing. As always past performance does not guarantee future returns.
Those lower stock prices have certainly provided some great topping up moments over the last year or more. The stock price has been falling, but the yields available on new purchases has gone from the sub 5% area to well over 6%. I made a few reinvestments over the last year as I prepared for my new semi retirement stage. The last purchase came on May 11th at a price of $42.80 Canadian. The yield purchased was 6.4%. So while Enbridge is not one of my largest Wide Moat 7 holdings by value, it is certainly delivering some of the healthier dividend payments. On the level of dividend it would follow Bell Canada ( BCE ), my biggest payer. While many were worried about the rising rates and the Spectra purchase execution, I simply kept buying. I bought my 15 of the largest cap Dividend Achievers 'without looking', and I do not judge or evaluate my Wide Moat 7. I trust the companies and management to deliver and execute. How would I know if Enbridge is going to be able to execute over the next 8-10 years (perhaps a suitable minimum time horizon for a stock investment for an investor). Management thinks they can turn the acquisition into another profit machine, or they would not have made the purchase. All said, I enjoy some of the commentary and guess work on the matter, and I was glad to see Michael Fitzimmons write this article suggesting that ENB had a 40% upside potential. Michael is an industry insider so I appreciate his opinion. Morningstar research also rated Enbridge 5 stars after the acquisition. Though I am not going to let an outside opinion overrule the opinion and strategy of management, or affect my investment decision. For a few years I have practiced buy and hold and add.
The timing of the dividend was of course a coincidence, but it provided the ammo for some cheeky emails to friends and family. I wrote ...
I did not work today on Day 1 of semi retirement, but I made a lot more today not working, compared to yesterday when I was working.
Unfortunately Enbridge won't be paying a dividend on Monday. But the timing could not have been more than perfect, and given that I do believe or have faith in Karma and 'signs from above' the healthy dividend was a clear message. Perhaps this will all work out. Five and one half years ago I more than cut my income in half to start my investment advisory 'career'. We moved into a negative cash flow situation for more than three years, but it all worked out in the end with promotions and salary increases, and I also created the role/job that I wanted. As former President Obama suggested in a recent speech, we should follow a purpose in our work, not seek a job title as the end goal. If we have a purpose in life and work the success has a better chance to follow. I believe Mr. Obama was alluding to karma, but not in so many words.
Maybe this will work again with me have cut my guaranteed income to zero. Once again, that dividend payment showed up to perhaps suggest I'm going to get a little help from my big juicy dividend payers until I get on my feet. There's some bond income on its way this week, and some of my US Dividend Achievers will be paying some modest dividends next week. And as my readers will know, I am not a fan of simply living off of the dividends. I will harvest dividends and I may also need to sell shares to create 'homemade dividends'. Selling shares allows us to tap the value in companies that pay those lesser dividends. It's one more tool, a needed tool for many, in the retirement funding stage. In fact, share harvesting created my first retirement income (in advance) as I sold some Apple shares ( OTC:APPL ) to fund my impending trip to Prince Edward Island. See my article This Summer, Apple is Taking Me To The Island, And Picking Up The Tab.
Happy Investing.
